survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports descriptive PISA 2022 results for Finland using the OECD PISA 2022 Database tables (e.g., I.B1.* for performance trends and I.B1.2.* for mean performance). The note does not specify the exact student sampling weight variable(s) or any replicate-weight scheme, but PISA estimates are produced under a complex sampling design with stratification and clustering at school and student levels. For analysts reproducing these estimates from microdata, the appropriate PISA sampling weights should be applied (and replicate weights used if variance estimation is required) following the PISA technical documentation. Because this document is a results factsheet rather than a microdata ML study, it does not provide enough information to confirm whether weights were explicitly applied in the computations shown here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a PISA 2022 results factsheet that reports proficiency levels, mean performance, and trend comparisons using OECD-published database tables rather than providing an explicit student-level modeling pipeline. Plausible values handling is therefore not applicable in the sense of not being described as a methodological choice in this factsheet (the OECD database tables already incorporate the PISA scaling approach). Missing-data handling is not reported because the factsheet does not describe any re-analysis of microdata or any imputation/deletion procedure; it only summarizes already-produced OECD estimates.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports Finland’s PISA 2022 analytic participation as 10,239 students in 241 schools who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading, or science, representing about 59,000 15-year-olds (estimated 95% of the total population of 15-year-olds). No additional inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., specific item subsets, grade restrictions beyond the 15-year-old target, or missing-data exclusions) are described in the factsheet; it presents the standard PISA 2022 reporting sample for Finland.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Finland factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Finland performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time. It reports mean performance trends (2012–2022 and 2018–2022), proficiency distributions (e.g., shares at Level 2+ and Level 5/6), and gaps by socio-economic status, gender, and immigrant background. The assessment used two two-hour tests with different students receiving different subject combinations, plus student and school questionnaires; results are drawn from the OECD PISA 2022 Database tables. Finland’s average performance is reported as higher than the OECD average in all three subjects, while declines from 2018 to 2022 are noted across subjects. The factsheet also highlights widening performance gaps by socio-economic status and differences by gender and immigrant background, but it does not provide an ML modeling framework, predictive metrics, or a microdata re-analysis methodology.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical ML paper and does not present a student-level predictive modeling design, algorithmic pipeline, or model performance metrics. It is a descriptive results factsheet based on OECD’s already-scaled PISA 2022 database tables, so fields related to ML techniques, plausible-value handling choices, and missing-data procedures are not reported as part of an analysis method. Consequently, main_findings and confounders_identified are intentionally empty because no ML targets/predictors are estimated in this document.
